title: Write a shippable prompt brief
summary: Turn a vague feature idea into a brief an agent can execute without guessing.
lesson: A good brief states the user, the job-to-be-done, and what done looks like.
Include constraints: stack, files you may touch, and what not to invent.
Add one acceptance check the agent can verify (route loads, test passes, form submits).
Prefer concrete nouns over vibes: “POST /api/events returns 202” beats “make it work.”

choices: Make the learning app cooler with AI vibes.
Add /launch that verifies a Ludwitt JWT and redirects to /learn when valid.
Use best practices for auth somehow.
quiz.explain: It names the route, the verification step, and the success redirect.

quiz.prompt: What should a brief tell the agent not to do?
choices: Invent deploy URLs or peer data that were not verified.
quiz.explain: Guardrails prevent confident fabrication.

quiz.prompt: Best acceptance check to include in a brief?
choices: “npm test passes and /learn returns 200 when signed in.”
quiz.explain: Verifiable outcomes beat subjective vibes.

title: Design a tiny API contract
summary: Specify routes, status codes, and payloads so agents and teammates don’t invent shapes.
lesson: Name the method + path first: POST /api/events, GET /api/health.
Document happy-path status codes (200/202) and auth failures (401/403).
Write one example JSON request and response — not a 20-field schema novel.
Keep secrets server-side; browsers call your proxy, not the upstream with the api key.

choices: POST /api/events → 202 { ok: true } when session is valid; 401 otherwise.
quiz.explain: Path, status, and auth condition are explicit.

quiz.prompt: Where should upstream API keys be used?
quiz.explain: Public exposure lets anyone impersonate your app.

choices: So agents and humans share the same field names
quiz.explain: Examples prevent invented field names.

title: Own the session cookie
summary: Know what belongs in an httpOnly session versus what must stay off the client.
lesson: After Ludwitt (or any IdP) succeeds, store user id + email in a signed httpOnly cookie.
Never put api keys, refresh secrets, or long-lived bearer tokens in localStorage for “ease.”
Bind server actions to the cookie session — ignore spoofed user_id from the request body.
Expire sessions; expired auth should send people back to sign-in, not silently invent a guest.

quiz.prompt: Safest place for a learning session identity?
quiz.explain: httpOnly + signature resists XSS theft and tampering.

choices: Trust it if the JSON parses
Overwrite with the session’s user id
Echo it into metrics for fun
Store it as the new api key
quiz.explain: Never trust client-supplied identity for privileged writes.

quiz.prompt: Refresh tokens for Ludwitt AI calls belong…
choices: In an httpOnly / server-only cookie store
quiz.explain: Tokens are secrets; keep them off the JS heap when possible.

title: Trust the Ludwitt launch JWT
summary: Validate launch tokens and reject anything that did not come from the launcher.
lesson: Ludwitt can redirect to /launch?token=… with a short-lived HS256 JWT.
Verify signature with jwt_secret, check exp, and confirm app_id matches your registration.
On failure, show a clear “sign in / launch” message — do not silently create a fake launched guest.
Store sub/email/session in an httpOnly cookie; never put api_key in that cookie.

choices: Be rejected with a clear launch-from-platform message
quiz.explain: Invalid tokens must not grant a learning session.

quiz.prompt: JWT payload field that identifies the Ludwitt user?
quiz.explain: sub is the platform user id used in event user_id.

quiz.prompt: If app_id in the token doesn’t match your registration…
choices: Rewrite the token in the browser
Treat it as a guest with XP
quiz.explain: Wrong app_id means the token wasn’t minted for you.

title: Instrument learning events
summary: Fire the right events so sessions count toward platform metrics.
lesson: Reuse one session id for every event in a visit.
Fire lesson_started when a module opens — not only on marketing page load.
Fire quiz_submitted when the learner answers; include score in metadata if useful.
Fire lesson_completed on the summary. Heartbeats alone do not qualify a session.

quiz.prompt: Minimum non-heartbeat signal for a valid learning session?
choices: At least one of lesson_started, quiz_submitted, or lesson_completed
quiz.explain: Platform pass evidence requires real learning events.

quiz.prompt: Where should the Ludwitt api_key live?
quiz.explain: Browser exposure would let anyone spoof events as your app.

choices: So progress/XP can credit the right module
quiz.explain: Progress systems key off module identity in metadata.

title: Ship a deploy smoke check
summary: Prove production is alive with a boring, reliable health check — not vibes.
lesson: Expose GET /api/health (or similar) that returns app identity and critical config flags — no secrets.
After every prod deploy, hit the health URL and the primary user path once.
Feature probes beat “it compiled”: signed-in /learn loading is stronger than a green build log.
When promoting links, prefer the marketplace/listing URL for counted users, not only the raw host.

choices: curl /api/health and open the signed-in practice path
quiz.explain: Production HTTP proof beats local compile confidence.
Useful for ops; never leak secrets.
Listing/launcher entry ties users to platform attribution.

title: Ship as part of a suite
summary: Connect learning to Market, PM, and Chat without fake SSO claims.
lesson: EudaLearn is the learning surface; EudaPM, EudaChat, and EudaMarket cover work, chat, and showcase.
Deep-link from Market /suite so people can find Learn — counted users should still enter via Ludwitt when required.
Be honest about auth: Ludwitt for Learn sessions; per-host cookies elsewhere — no invented cross-app SSO.
One suite story beats four orphan demos: shared brand, clear handoffs, real links.

choices: Only the raw Vercel URL in a private gist
quiz.explain: Launcher entry ties users to platform metrics.

quiz.prompt: What should you avoid claiming across Euda apps?
choices: That they are one product suite for the pilot
That they share a single SSO cookie across every host
That learners should prefer the Ludwitt listing for counted use
quiz.explain: Auth is per host / Ludwitt launch — don’t invent SSO.

choices: A broken iframe with no link
A clear CTA to the Learn listing/login
Asking users to guess the subdomain
quiz.explain: Explicit CTAs are how distribution works.

title: Close the feedback loop
summary: Use coach tips, quizzes, and human review without treating any single signal as absolute truth.
lesson: Automated coach tips are suggestions — schema-validate model output and degrade if the proxy fails.
Quiz explanations teach the rule; scores alone don’t prove mastery.
For product work, prefer written review + a live deploy over emoji reactions.
When credits are empty, keep the core lesson usable — never block learning on the tip.

quiz.prompt: If the AI coach returns 402 insufficient credits…
choices: Show a calm message and continue with the explanation
quiz.explain: Core practice must work when the smart layer is off.

choices: A thumbs-up emoji with no link
A written note plus a working deploy URL
quiz.explain: Review + live proof beats empty praise.

choices: Piped straight to the UI with no checks
Used to skip the quiz entirely
quiz.explain: Untrusted model text needs a guardrail.
